metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [August 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.159

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [August 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.159
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.159
- Datum: 08.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah, we start this
letter on board of the ship, the rest will
follow from Rio where we hope to
find your news. I am
sorry to say it but we are frightfully spoiled
here on the ship and it is the most wonderful
voyage one can imagine - I wish you had
only one day out of our twelve, The air
warm and a marvellous breeze all day,
Sunbaths and waterbathes, nice people,
Brazilians, Argentines, Suisse, Dutch which
all are good and old readers of my books
from tomorrow (after Barbados) I
shall get a state cabin to work in. It
was really necessary and a rest after
the hot days of Newyork, where poor
Lotte finally nearly broke down - I have
done there hard work to make some
money, minor but amusing work and
we had to see many people, Unfortuna
tely just the last two days, when you
cabled about Heiner were the worst, I
had to see a doctor on behalf of an
attack of sciatica and some other thing

[Randnotiz links, von unten nach oben geschrieben:]
just recieved your telegram as board
in your [?]

[Stempel oben links:]
AMERICAN
The Good
Neighbor
Fleet
REPUBLIC
LINE

[Gedruckter Text oben rechts:]
VIA AIR MAIL
ON BOARD
S. S. Argentina
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Die Randnotiz links ist vertikal geschrieben. Der Stempel 'American Republic Line' ist teilweise über den Text gedruckt.

pages.transcription:
Lotte lost a filling and had to rush to a
dentist, than we had to go to the Custom
House and when our ship left Lotte was
so tired, that she remained the whole
next day to bed, But what a splendid
rest cure we have and I suppose that
Brazil will not remain behind our
expectations. Our friends expect us
there in the kindest way and I have
invitations for lectures from Uruguay
Argentine, Chile, Venezuela; I suppose
all will go all right and we would
be perfectly happy as seldom in a
voyage would not the idea of the
war destroy much of our feelings.
We get on the ship nearly no news
just a few lines - The Americans
are terribly indifferent to all what
happens, they help but they have not
the right compassion and not enough
foresight - we were glad to leave
Newyork because we could not stand
longer this "jolly mess" in such a time

[Randnotiz links, von unten nach oben geschrieben:]
Now Lotte will write you more, kindest regards
Stefan

[Randnotiz rechts, von oben nach unten geschrieben:]
We have charming people on board, all the ambassadors of the [?] are
my chess partners
pages.notes: Fortsetzung des Briefes. Randnotizen links und rechts vertikal geschrieben. Die Lesung der Randnotiz rechts ist aufgrund der Handschrift und des Platzmangels teilweise unsicher.
Farbskala und Grauskala für Archivierung. Der Ausschnitt des Briefes ist eine Wiederholung von Seite 2.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist weitgehend gut lesbar. Einige Wörter in den Randnotizen sind aufgrund der vertikalen Ausrichtung und der engen Platzierung leicht unsicher, aber im Kontext verständlich.
